messages:
maria: Quick sanity check — I'm seeing a sustained p95 jump for the `gen-api` route starting ~09:10 UTC, tokens/sec steady. Before I escalate, which dashboards/metrics/traces are the fastest to check for root cause?

alex: Start with the gen-api latency dashboard (front-end + gpu pool panels). Grafana: https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/abc123/gen-api (panels: p50/p95/p99, request rate, queue depth). Also open Jaeger: https://jaeger.internal.redwood/search?service=gen-api for traces.

alex: Quick promql snippets I use:
```
# p95 for gen-api (histogram_quantile over request_duration_seconds)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="gen-api"}[5m])) by (le))

# tokens/sec across gen-backend workers
sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total{job=~"gen-backend.*"}[1m]))
```

alex: If tokens/sec is flat but p95 rises, check queue length, concurrency, and KV/cache hit-rate. Also look for tails in model GPU exec time: `model_exec_pxx` panels.

jin: +1 on queue length. Check `gen_api_inflight_requests` and `worker_queue_depth` panels. If inflight climbs but workers aren't scaling, that's likely an autoscaler or resource constraint.

sam: Also verify recent deploys — could be a regressed kernel or quantization change. @devbot, show last deploy for gen-api in last 2 hours.

devbot: deploy-bot: gen-api v3.14.2 promoted to prod at 2028-07-05T09:04:12Z by @ci (sha: d4f8a2e). No rollbacks recorded.

maria: OK — no recent rollback. I pulled a few traces: some requests show long GC-ish pauses on the host before model exec. Where are the infra logs for worker pods?

alex: Logs are in Loki: query `{job="gen-backend"} |= "oom" or |= "pause"` and filter by pod label. Grafana panel "worker logs (loki)" links directly to the query.

alex: If you want a single checklist: 1) p95/p99 panels (5m/1m windows) 2) tokens/sec + request rate 3) inflight/queue depth 4) model_exec_pxx and GPU utilization 5) Loki logs for pauses/OOMs 6) Jaeger traces for slow spans.

sam: For alerts — current p95 alert is `p95(gen_api_request_duration) > 800ms for 5m`. We might need to tune to 10m or add a tokens/sec clause to avoid noisy alerts on short spikes. Example:
```
expr: (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="gen-api"}[5m])) by (le)) > 0.8)
and on() (sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total{job="gen-backend"}[5m])) > 10)
for: 10m
```

jin: That AND clause is handy — avoids alerting when traffic is zero. Also consider alerting on sustained increase in queue depth.

maria: Super helpful. I'll check queue metrics + logs first. If I see host GC/OOMs I'll open an incident. Thanks! :thumbsup:

alex: Ping me if you need direct links, I'll drop them.

maria: Quick one more — where's the canonical doc that defines our p50/p95/p99 measurement windows and calculation? Want to cite it in the incident note.

jin: There's a short doc in the observability repo: https://git.internal.redwood/observability/latency-metrics.md — it defines the histograms, quantile windows, and recommended panels.

maria: Perfect. I'll follow up with a short runbook if this reproduces. Thanks all.

sam: thx, and fyi I can tweak the alert after you confirm persistence.

maria: Will do — marking this as resolved for now unless new signs show up. :white_check_mark:
